catalog_quote: [1980: vi] Biyom and Tauya are closer related to each other than to the two other members of the group. ... Isabi and Biyom languages are tonal and they are the only tonal languages so far known within the Adelbert Range language group. [1980: viii-ix, §9] The transcription of the wordlist is rendered semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted and fluctuating sounds were transcribed consistently only when discovered early enough to make the transcription uniform. new_statements.quote: Isabi and Biyom languages are tonal and they are the only tonal languages so far known within the Adelbert Range language group. [1980: vi] — earlier, more hedged: Biyom was originally believed to be linked with the Gende language and the East New Guinea Highlands Stock. The language appears to be tonal. [1975a: 585]
new_statements.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: Australian National University.
new_statements.locator: Introduction, §3 'The Brahman languages', p. vi (PDF page 6 of the ANU open-access file); corroborated by Z'graggen 1975, 'The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum', §2.8.2.2.2.6, p. 585 (p. 17 of)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (114 pp., text present, ANU open-access PL-D33). p. 6 = printed p. vi, Introduction §3 'The Brahman languages': the passage reads (scanned letter-spacing removed) 'Isabi and Biyom languages are tonal and they are the only tonal languages so far known within the Adelbert Range language group.' Exactly as quoted. Immediately before it: 'Biyom and Tauya are closer related to each other than to the two other members of the group' and the Deibler (SIL) personal-communication remark on Isabi/Gahuku. §9 (pp. viii-ix) says the transcription is 'semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted' and lists for Biyom only segmental fluctuations (r~d, v~w~b, nd~nj, s~z)…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given anywhere. Z'graggen, the only linguist to have collected Biyom data, reports from his 1973 survey that Biyom (with Isabi) is a tone language, the only tonal languages he knew of in the Adelbert Range group; he says nothing about stress or accent, marks neither tone nor stress in the ~300-item wordlist, and describes his transcription as semi-phonemic with non-contrastive phonetic detail omitted.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the tone claim is an unanalysed survey impression ('appears to be tonal' in 1975, stated flatly in 1980) with no tonemes, minimal pairs or examples given.
new_statements.domain_note: Survey-level typological remark on the language as a whole, based on wordlist elicitation of isolated citation forms; no word- vs phrase-level discussion. No phonological description of Biyom exists in any source located.
new_statements.identity_note: Z'graggen's 'Biyom (Sasime/Sasimo)', code I2 in his Brahman family (with Isabi, Tauya, Faita), 379 speakers in 1975 in Omkwisi, Promesi (Tomo), Yaikoro (Bium) and Yomika villages, south-central Madang Province; this is the same entity as Glottolog biyo1244 / ISO bpm. No dialects are distinguished in any source. Note Glottolog files Biyom under Rai Coast (unclassified) whereas Z'graggen treats it as Adelbert Range (Brahman); the tone remark applies to the language as a whole.

sources.note: Tauya is Biyom's closest relative ('Biyom and Tauya are closer related to each other than to the two other members of the group', Z'graggen 1980: vi); the only full grammar in the Brahman group, so the nearest description of the prosodic type and the likeliest place for an aside on Biyom. Not a Biyom source itself.
